paragraphs.text: Our cohort analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that LMO7 is disturbed as shown here.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: In several cancer models, loss or dysregulation of LMO7 can alter cell morphology, migration, invasion, and EMT-associated programs (Zhen et al. (2022); Zeng et al. (2024); Liu et al. (2021)). In addition, LMO7 has been implicated in the organization and remodeling of embryonic epithelial tissues through its role in apical junctional complexes and actomyosin-dependent epithelial morphogenesis (Matsuda et al. (2022)).

sections.heading: Pathway

paragraphs.suffix: (LMO7, SNAI1, CDH1). LMO7 is positioned as a contributor to epithelial cell-cell adhesion. Adherens junctions depend on both cell-cell recognition/adhesion and mechanical coupling to the actin cytoskeleton, with LMO7 contributing primarily to the latter. Through interactions with afadin and α-actinin, LMO7 helps organize the actin network associated with adherens junctions, thereby supporting the stabilization and maintenance of epithelial cell-cell contacts.

paragraphs: The extended pathway diagram shows how LMO7 is placed. It supports Epithelial Cell-Cell Adhesion leading to EMT but in parallel to the known regulatory path SNAI1-CDH1-Epithelial Cell-Cell Adhesion-Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT).
